properties.name: v0.38.0 was tagged with an empty INCLUDES manifest because release_includes_all defaults to a dry run and its success reads identically
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-21, in the v0.38.0 cut, and found only because a completeness audit was run AFTER the tag was already pushed.

`release_includes_all` **defaults to a DRY RUN** (`apply: false`). Its response says so — the payload carries `"applied": false` beside `"added": 304`. I called it twice, checked `isError` both times, saw no error and the number 304, and moved on. **v0.38.0 was tagged, built, published and verified with an EMPTY manifest: 0 INCLUDES edges against v0.37.0's 275.**

⭐ THE DEFAULT IS RIGHT AND IS NOT THE DEFECT. Its own description gives the reason: "the derivation is reported and nothing is written, so you can read what a release is about to package before you package it." A tool that writes 304 edges on a bare call would be worse. The dry run is a good design.

🛑 THE DEFECT IS THAT A DRY RUN AND A WRITE ARE INDISTINGUISHABLE TO EVERY CHECK THAT RAN. `isError` was false in both cases — correctly, since nothing failed. `added: 304` reads as an accomplishment and is actually a FORECAST. And the release's own gates all passed over the empty manifest: `reflow2_check` OK, `release_report` was never called, and nothing anywhere asks whether a Release about to ship has any INCLUDES at all.

📌 THIS IS `rule:success-is-read-from-the-authoritative-object` FAILING ON A NEW SURFACE. That rule was written for `gh pr merge`, whose local half fails while the merge lands — read the PR object, not the CLI. The same shape here: the authoritative object is the RELEASE (`release_report` returns 215 artifacts / 89 components / 190 capabilities when it worked, and `artifacts: []` when it had not), and I read the CALL instead.

⇒ TWO REMEDIES, NEITHER BUILT:
  (1) A DETECTOR: a Release with an AT_EPOCH edge, a deploy, and ZERO INCLUDES is a release record that claims to have shipped nothing. Nothing reports it. It sits beside the known sibling `nothing detects a Release with no epoch`, and it is the same class.
  (2) The release procedure should END by reading `release_report`, not by reading the last write's return value. A cut is verified the way the published assets are verified — off the object, after the fact.

📌 CORRECTED THE SAME DAY: re-run with `apply: true`, 304 edges written, `release_report` now returns 215/89/190. The tag and the published binaries were never wrong; only the design's record of what they contained was.
